summary:
Astronaut health are inherently biopsychosocial, as such they experience health problems that are interconnected with one another during space mission.
the pain point is lack of timely integrated monitoring tool, inadequate technology that can predict a disease before it occurrences.
we propose a smart integrated monitoring device addressing human being as a whole for predictive, preventive and personalized astronaut well being using Iot and AI-Powered capable of predicting a disease, offering warning sign before some one breakdown and suffer irreversible health problem.
details:
MotivAid is an AI- and IoT-powered health intelligence system that monitors astronaut wellbeing continuously and flags problems early. It is built on Engel's Biopsychosocial Model and tracks three domains: HEART (cardiovascular status), SLEEP (sleep quality and recovery) and MIND (stress and mood).

How it works:A wearable captures physiological signals and sends them by Bluetooth Low Energy to an onboard computing device. The interface runs an AI analysis that produces a personalised health risk score, if high risk it will ignite danger sign(Red). The astronaut gets alerts and self-guidance. A clinician web dashboard shows the same data, so the earth based medical team can review trends and make a medical decision. Feedback returns to the astronaut and refines their personal baseline, and monitoring continues onboard.

Benefits and intended impact: Long missions expose crew to cardiovascular strain, disrupted sleep and psychological stress, and conventional checks are periodic and reactive. MotivAid shifts care to proactive, preventive and personalised, so risks are caught before they become emergencies. It also supports autonomous care when communication with Earth is delayed. The same approach could serve remote and undeserved communities on Earth.

Tools, hardware and software: The prototype is a web application deployed on GitHub Pages, running on simulated data. The wearable concept intend using an ESP32-WROOM-32, a MAX30102 heart-rate sensor, a piezoelectric respiration sensor, a Grove GSR sensor, an MPU6050 motion sensor, and cortisol bioreceptors (C-Mab, aptamers, MIPs) with an LMP91000 potentiostat and an ADS1115 16-bit ADC. ECG and a mood-log module (speaker and camera) are planned additions. but now existing smart watch are used, the AI for health problem prediction will use python, specifically XGBoost

Creativity: It combines physical, sleep and psychological monitoring in one platform instead of treating them separately. perform AI deep analysis using mathmatical modelling equation to predict the likelihood of disease occurences in the clinician dash board.It also propose biochemical stress sensing through cortisol and a personalized baseline for each astronaut.

Factors considered: Astronaut privacy, data security, sensor accuracy and calibration, comfort of the wearable, limited bandwidth in space, clinical validation, and the fact that the prototype is not a medical device.
